definition: Tidewater Georgian, offered as the place to begin: a variant of Georgian Colonial American, the first style the corpus filled end to end, read whole in its dossier, with an example brief to compose a house from.
more: The example stops at the brief, and on evidence: its house has no plan that places. The plan written for it is refused because its placement breaks facts of its own house type, and an attempt to write one that places found the fact that decides it. With the dining room's fire on the west gable beside the drawing room's, where the massing's paired end chimneys put it, the dining room must span the whole west range to reach the passage, and the butler's pantry that opens off it is left no place inside its own size bands. The dining room's own record puts that fire on an interior wall instead, and it has since been ruled that the style's own statement governs: its kit puts every hearth on a gable end, so the plan follows the gable and the house is refused on its own facts. No sheet or export of it is drawn, and the plan step names the conflict instead.
basis: Editorial. Which style is offered as the guided example is the workbench's own choice for Phase 14, and no corpus file names one; what the style is, is the corpus's. README.md: "Georgian Colonial is filled end to end" as its depth-first proof, and "Tidewater Georgian is then written as a" short override of it, "each resolving the rest from the parent". The example brief is briefs/family-georgian.json, the one docs/compose.md runs first. Where the example stops, in its more: build/typefacts.py, the refusal to draw: "a placement that breaks a hard fact of the type is REFUSED, not" drawn; and build/revise.py, the corrective loop, on a placement already refused when it starts: "refused -> refused on a lower key is accepted, which is the Tidewater plan's own case". Why no plan of it places, which an attempt to write one measured: massings/catalog.json, the four-over-four: "Paired end chimneys serve four fireplaces per floor."; partis/centre-passage-double-pile.json: "A through-passage front to back with two rooms either side"; rooms/butlers-pantry.json, on where the pantry stands: "the pantry is in the block and the kitchen is in another building"; and rooms/dining-room.json, on where its own fire stands: "Historically a fireplace on the interior wall opposite the sideboard". Which of the two governs, as ruled: kits/tidewater-georgian.kit.json, the style's own hearth: "Hearths are at the gable ends, on the outside walls of the end rooms". The arithmetic that joins them, the variants tried and the other ways the example could have been answered are in the report on the attempt and in the open questions on the worked house and on the dining fire's wall, which a glossary basis may not quote.
